name: FCP AI-Toolkit
hardwareRequirementCaveat: Apple Silicon is the documented target and qualification platform. No independently verified exact minimum chip or RAM requirement is available; do not invent M1-only or RAM minimum claims.

pricing.templates: Five Motion title templates are free to install and use in Final Cut Pro. Once installed, they can be used without the companion app running.
pricing.ai: Automatic AI caption and subtitle generation requires an active monthly subscription.
pricing.priceGuidance: See the Mac App Store and in-app purchase sheet for current regional subscription pricing and terms.

releasedFeatures: Native Final Cut Pro workflow extension
Subtitles grouped into a compound clip within a secondary storyline
Smart Cache reuses transcribed media ranges (same media, language and model) and transcribes only missing ranges; on by default, can be turned off
Persistent in-extension caption text, start time and end time edits, with a remove button per caption
Smart Search across locally cached captions, including saved text corrections
About 100 Whisper-model language codes and local Auto Detect
Extension layout fits smaller Final Cut Pro windows

privacy.audioProcessing: After a model is downloaded, transcription and Auto Detect run locally on the Mac.
privacy.transcriptionUpload: The implemented transcription path uses local audio files with WhisperKit rather than uploading audio to a cloud transcription service.
privacy.modelDownload: Whisper model downloads require network access. The app uses WhisperKit and the argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml model repository.
privacy.purchases: Apple StoreKit handles product information, purchases, entitlement verification, and purchase restoration.
privacy.localStorage: The app stores model files, preferences, selected-folder access bookmarks, and subscription state locally. Smart Cache (1.1.1) stores cached transcripts, caption corrections, and search data in a local App Group database shared by the app and its extension.
avoidClaims: The application never uses the internet
No data of any kind is ever collected by anyone
All languages have been individually quality tested
Website hosting has no server logs
A third-party privacy or security audit has been completed
privacy.policyStatus: The website privacy page describes verified behavior and distinguishes the application, website hosting (Cloudflare, GitHub Pages backup), model downloads, and Apple purchases. No audited retention or website hosting-log policy has been located.

languageCaveat: 100 languages describes the Whisper model catalog. Quality has not been separately validated for every language.
searchCaveat: Search results show text, source filename, and timecode. Direct navigation to Final Cut Pro clips is not part of 1.1.
notIncluded: SRT or other standard subtitle-file export
AI Motion graph generation or editing

release111.whyNot11: 1.1 was finished and checked on 2026-09-22 but never released publicly. On 2026-09-25 a final test on real projects found two bugs; both were fixed the same day and the build was renumbered 1.1.1 (1.1 features plus two fixes).
fixes: Overlapping duplicate captions that could lock the caption editor (captions trimmed to each clip's visible timeline range, duplicate speech merged, remaining overlaps split, older caches repaired on load, remove-caption button added)

Caption timing for detached and connected audio (correct timeline positions for nested and connected clips, connected clips bounded by their storyline, video not treated as audio, roles, disabled clips and inactive audio channels respected)
release111.notes: The window clipping fixed for smaller Final Cut Pro windows appeared during 1.1 development; 1.0 did not have it. The caption editor is new in 1.1.1, so no public user met the locked editor.
